questions.stem: A report must answer questions as fast as possible, and the business is content with figures that are refreshed once each night. Which storage mode fits best?
options: Import
DirectQuery
Dual
A live connection to the source system
questions.answer: Import
questions.explanation: Import loads a compressed copy of the data into memory, which is what makes it the fastest mode for queries. Its cost is that the data is only as fresh as the last refresh, and a nightly refresh is exactly the case where that cost does not matter.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: A Product dimension is used both by an imported summary table and by a very large DirectQuery detail table. Which storage mode should the dimension use?
options: Dual
Import
DirectQuery
Direct Lake
questions.answer: Dual
questions.explanation: A dual table is cached like an import table and can also be queried at the source like a DirectQuery table, and the engine chooses per query. That is what stops a shared dimension forcing every query against the imported summary to go out to the source, which is the usual reason a composite model performs worse than expected.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: What makes Direct Lake different from both Import and DirectQuery when reading a Delta table in a lakehouse?
options: It loads the Delta files straight into memory without keeping a separate copy and without translating DAX into SQL
It keeps a compressed copy of the data exactly as Import does, but refreshes it more often
It translates every DAX query into T-SQL and sends it to the SQL analytics endpoint
It requires the tables to be converted from Delta into a proprietary format first
questions.answer: It loads the Delta files straight into memory without keeping a separate copy and without translating DAX into SQL
questions.explanation: Direct Lake reads the Delta parquet files in OneLake directly, so it avoids the duplication and refresh window of Import and also avoids the query translation and source round trip of DirectQuery. Understanding that it is neither of the other two, rather than a faster version of one of them, is the point of this skill.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Choose a storage mode

questions.stem: You are asked to describe the shape of a star schema to a colleague who has only ever seen flat spreadsheets. What is the arrangement?
options: One central fact table of measurable events, surrounded by dimension tables that describe them
One table per report page, each holding everything that page needs
A chain of tables where each one relates only to the next
Several fact tables joined directly to each other
questions.answer: One central fact table of measurable events, surrounded by dimension tables that describe them
questions.explanation: A star schema puts the events being measured in a fact table and the things being described, such as product, customer and date, in dimension tables related to it. The name comes from the shape this produces on a diagram, and the arrangement is what allows a filter on any dimension to propagate cleanly into the facts.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: A model contains Product related to Subcategory, which is in turn related to Category. What does star schema guidance recommend doing with those three tables?
options: Flatten them into a single Product dimension carrying subcategory and category as columns
Leave them as they are, because more tables always mean better compression
Relate Category directly to the fact table as well
Turn Subcategory into a second fact table
questions.answer: Flatten them into a single Product dimension carrying subcategory and category as columns
questions.explanation: Product, Subcategory and Category form a snowflake, and the usual advice is to denormalise them into one dimension. It shortens the filter path from the attribute the user picks to the fact table, and it removes tables that mean nothing on their own from the field list.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: A sales fact has both an order date and a ship date, and both need to be sliced by the same date dimension. What is the standard way to model that?
options: Keep one active relationship and activate the other inside a measure with USERELATIONSHIP
Make both relationships active at the same time
Remove the date dimension and use the raw date columns on the fact
Set the second relationship to filter in both directions
questions.answer: Keep one active relationship and activate the other inside a measure with USERELATIONSHIP
questions.explanation: This is a role-playing dimension. Only one relationship between two tables can be active, so the second is created as inactive and switched on for the measures that need it using USERELATIONSHIP inside CALCULATE. The alternative, duplicating the date table, is also valid but costs a second table the user has to understand.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement a star schema for a semantic model

questions.stem: Each customer can hold several accounts and each account can be held by several customers. What do you add to the model to relate them?
options: A bridge table with one row per customer and account pair
A direct relationship between the two tables filtering both ways
A calculated column on each table holding the other table's key
A second copy of the customer table
questions.answer: A bridge table with one row per customer and account pair
questions.explanation: A genuine many-to-many needs a table in the middle holding the valid combinations, so that each side has an ordinary one-to-many relationship to the bridge. Trying to relate the two tables directly either fails or produces an ambiguous model that gives wrong totals.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: A colleague has set every relationship in the model to filter in both directions because it made one visual work. Why is that a bad default?
options: It can create ambiguous filter paths and slow queries down
It prevents the model from ever being refreshed
It converts the model to DirectQuery automatically
It removes the ability to write measures
questions.answer: It can create ambiguous filter paths and slow queries down
questions.explanation: Bidirectional filtering is a targeted tool, not a default. Applied everywhere it can leave more than one path between two tables, which makes the result of a filter ambiguous, and it forces the engine to do more work. It is worth enabling deliberately for a specific need, such as a bridge table, and not otherwise.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: Two tables already have one active relationship, and you create a second one between the same pair. What does the model do with it?
options: It is created as inactive, and only a measure that names it can use it
It replaces the first relationship
It is created active, and the engine picks whichever suits each query
It is rejected and cannot be created at all
questions.answer: It is created as inactive, and only a measure that names it can use it
questions.explanation: Only one relationship in a path between two tables can be active, so a second is stored but dormant. Nothing uses it until a calculation asks for it explicitly, which is both the constraint and the mechanism behind role-playing dimensions.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement relationships, such as bridge tables and many-to-many relationships

questions.stem: The same subexpression appears three times in one measure. What is the main benefit of assigning it to a DAX variable first?
options: It is evaluated once and reused, which is both clearer and usually faster
It forces the measure to be recalculated on every visual
It converts the measure into a calculated column
It allows the measure to ignore all filters
questions.answer: It is evaluated once and reused, which is both clearer and usually faster
questions.explanation: A variable is evaluated once, at the point it is declared, and its result is reused wherever the name appears. That removes repeated work and gives the expression a name that says what it means, which is why variables are the first thing to reach for in any measure longer than a line.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: Revenue must be calculated by multiplying quantity by unit price on each individual sales row and then totalling the result. Which kind of DAX function does that?
options: An iterator such as SUMX, which evaluates an expression row by row
A simple aggregation such as SUM over a single column
An information function such as ISBLANK
A filter modifier such as REMOVEFILTERS
questions.answer: An iterator such as SUMX, which evaluates an expression row by row
questions.explanation: Multiplying two columns and then adding up the results is not the same as multiplying two totals, so the calculation has to happen per row. Iterators walk a table and evaluate an expression in each row context, which is exactly that. SUM can only add one column that already exists.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: A measure needs the value from the previous row in whatever order the visual is currently sorted by. Which family of DAX functions is designed for that?
options: Window functions such as OFFSET, which navigate relative to the current row of a result
Time intelligence functions, which are the only way to look backwards
Information functions, which report on the current filter context
Filter modifiers, which change which rows are visible
questions.answer: Window functions such as OFFSET, which navigate relative to the current row of a result
questions.explanation: Window functions operate over a result set and can address rows relative to the current one, which is what a previous-row comparison needs when the ordering is the visual's rather than a calendar's. Time intelligence handles the calendar case specifically and cannot express an arbitrary sort order.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Write calculations that use DAX variables and functions, such as iterators, table filtering, windowing, and information functions

questions.stem: Forty measures each need year to date, prior year and year over year variants, and nobody wants to write a hundred and twenty measures. What solves this?
options: A calculation group holding one calculation item per variant
Forty more measures, generated with a script
A field parameter listing the forty measures
A dynamic format string on each measure
questions.answer: A calculation group holding one calculation item per variant
questions.explanation: A calculation group defines each variant once as a calculation item that rewrites whatever measure it is applied to. Three items then cover all forty measures, and adding a forty first measure needs no extra work. Generating the measures with a script produces the same behaviour and leaves a hundred and twenty things to maintain.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: One measure must display as currency when the user selects an amount and as a percentage when they select a ratio. What makes a single measure do that?
options: A dynamic format string, which is a DAX expression returning the format
Two measures and a bookmark for each state
A conditional formatting rule on the visual
A calculated column holding the formatted text
questions.answer: A dynamic format string, which is a DAX expression returning the format
questions.explanation: A dynamic format string lets the format itself be a DAX expression evaluated in the current context, so one measure can present as currency, percentage or anything else depending on what is selected. Returning formatted text from a calculated column produces a string, which then sorts and aggregates as text rather than as a number.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: Users want to choose from a slicer whether a chart is broken down by product, region or channel, without you building three charts. What provides that?
options: A field parameter, which exposes a chosen set of fields as a slicer
A calculation group with one item per breakdown
A bookmark for each breakdown, wired to buttons
Row-level security roles for each breakdown
questions.answer: A field parameter, which exposes a chosen set of fields as a slicer
questions.explanation: Field parameters turn a list of columns or measures into a table that can be put in a slicer, so the axis or the value of a visual becomes the user's choice. Calculation groups swap the calculation rather than the field, and bookmarks would need one saved state per combination and would not scale.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement calculation groups, dynamic format strings, and field parameters

questions.stem: What does turning on the large semantic model storage format actually change about a model?
options: It lets the model grow beyond the default size limit, up to the limit of the capacity
It compresses the data more aggressively so the model becomes smaller
It moves the model out of memory and onto disk permanently
It converts every table in the model to DirectQuery
questions.answer: It lets the model grow beyond the default size limit, up to the limit of the capacity
questions.explanation: The setting changes the storage format the service uses for the model so that it is no longer bound by the default per-model size limit and can grow to what the capacity allows. It does not change how the data itself is compressed and it does not change any table's storage mode.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: Which of these is a genuine reason to put a semantic model into the large storage format?
options: The model is expected to exceed the default size limit as history accumulates
The report pages take too long to render
The source system is slow to query during refresh
The model needs row-level security
questions.answer: The model is expected to exceed the default size limit as history accumulates
questions.explanation: The setting is about size, so the use case is a model that will outgrow the default limit. Slow visuals are a report and DAX problem, a slow source is a data preparation problem, and row-level security works regardless of storage format. Reaching for a capacity setting to fix a modelling problem is a common and expensive detour.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: A colleague plans to enable large semantic model storage format on every model in the tenant on the grounds that bigger is safer. What is the honest counterargument?
options: It is a size setting with no query benefit, so applying it everywhere adds capacity pressure for nothing
It permanently prevents those models from being deleted
It disables incremental refresh on every model it is applied to
It requires every report to be rebuilt against the model
questions.answer: It is a size setting with no query benefit, so applying it everywhere adds capacity pressure for nothing
questions.explanation: The setting removes a ceiling; it does not make anything faster. Enabling it blindly across a tenant means the models that never needed it gain nothing while the capacity carries the consequences of larger models being allowed to exist. Settings that only remove a limit should be applied where the limit is actually being met.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Identify use cases for and configure large semantic model storage format

questions.stem: What makes a semantic model a composite model rather than an ordinary one?
options: It combines tables in more than one storage mode, or from more than one source
It contains more than one fact table
It has been deployed through more than one workspace
It uses calculation groups as well as measures
questions.answer: It combines tables in more than one storage mode, or from more than one source
questions.explanation: Composite is about mixing: import tables alongside DirectQuery tables, or tables drawn from separate sources including other semantic models. Several fact tables in one storage mode is just a normal model, and how a model is deployed has nothing to do with it.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models

questions.stem: You want to extend the certified enterprise sales model with a small budget table of your own, without copying the enterprise model or asking its owners to change it. What do you build, and what do you need?
options: A composite model on top of the enterprise model, which requires Build permission on it
A copy of the enterprise model, which requires Write permission on it
A DirectQuery connection to the enterprise model's underlying warehouse instead
A dataflow that reloads the enterprise model's tables into your workspace
questions.answer: A composite model on top of the enterprise model, which requires Build permission on it
questions.explanation: A composite model can take a connection to an existing semantic model and add local tables beside it, which keeps one governed definition of sales while letting you add what only you need. Build permission is what allows that connection. Copying or reloading the tables forks the definition, which is the outcome the enterprise model exists to prevent.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models

questions.stem: A composite model holds a huge DirectQuery fact table and a small imported table of the same figures summarised by month. How do you make queries use the small one whenever they can?
options: Configure the imported table as a user-defined aggregation over the detail table
Hide the DirectQuery table so users cannot pick it
Set the imported table to dual storage mode
Add a bidirectional relationship between the two tables
questions.answer: Configure the imported table as a user-defined aggregation over the detail table
questions.explanation: Aggregations tell the engine that a small cached table can answer certain queries in place of a large one, and it then redirects to it automatically and falls back to the detail table when the query is too granular. Hiding a table changes what users see rather than what the engine does.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Design and build composite models
